plan: My private value is $9. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I risk paying more than my value if I win. Since the values are independently drawn and this is a one-round game, I'll bid close to my true value to maximize potential profit.

My private value is $9. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is usually to bid my true value. If I bid less than $9, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more than $9, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. Since this is a one-round game with no repeated interactions, bidding exactly my value ($9) seems most rational.

With a private value of $34, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since this is a single round with no prior history, I'll use a strategic bid slightly below my true value. By bidding around $33-$34, I increase my chances of winning while ensuring I only pay less than my value. This strategy protects my potential profit margin. I'll bid just under my true value to create a buffer that allows me to win if others bid lower, but prevents overpaying.
